topics.titleTr: Bir Haftalık Reels için ChatGPT İş Akışı
topics.titleEn: A ChatGPT Workflow for a Week of Reels
topics.angle: how-to|a repeatable ChatGPT process to plan, script and caption a week of Reels in one sitting.
topics.brief: Practical field-notes workflow for a solo creator. Sections: feed ChatGPT a brand/voice brief once and reuse it; generate a week of hooks from one content pillar; turn each hook into a 20-second script and shot list; batch captions and keyword-aware on-screen text; a human editing pass so it doesn't read as AI. Note the research point that vague prompts yield generic output, so inputs must be specific. Verify any cited feature. Primary sources: OpenAI Academy marketing use-cases; Metricool ChatGPT-for-social guide.

topics.titleTr: ChatGPT'de Bir Aylık Pazarlama Metnini Hazırla
topics.titleEn: Batch a Month of Marketing Copy in ChatGPT
topics.angle: how-to|batch-produce a month of on-brand marketing copy in a single structured ChatGPT session.
topics.brief: Show a batching session that beats one-off prompting. Sections: a prompt scaffold (role, context, task, format, constraints) reused per asset; generating a month of emails, ad variants and landing blurbs from one campaign brief; keeping voice consistent with a pasted brand profile or custom GPT; a QA checklist before anything ships; where ChatGPT shouldn't go (analytics, attribution, real-time campaign calls). Verify the prompt-structure and limits framing. Primary sources: Dupple 2026 ChatGPT-for-marketing guide; ClickUp marketing use-cases; OpenAI Academy.

topics.titleTr: Okur AI Metnini Anlıyor: Güveni Geri Kazan
topics.titleEn: Readers Can Smell AI Copy. Win Trust Back
topics.angle: mistakes|the tells that expose AI copy and how to edit for credibility and voice.
topics.brief: Contrarian push against publish-as-generated. Sections: the data that skepticism is rising (Metricool: the share of marketers saying AI performs worse than human work rose from 5% in 2025 to 14% in 2026); the tells (hedging, symmetrical lists, no specifics, no POV); an editing pass that adds first-hand detail, real examples, opinion and rhythm; disclosure and the platform AI-label trend. Verify the 5%-to-14% figure. Primary sources: Metricool ChatGPT-for-marketing report; Dupple mistakes section.

topics.titleTr: 1X Neo: 20 Bin Dolarlık Ev Robotu Hazır mı?
topics.titleEn: 1X Neo: Is a $20K Home Robot Ready in 2026?
topics.angle: deep-dive|assess whether 1X's $20K Neo humanoid is a real home product or an early demo.
topics.brief: Use the CES-2026 era humanoid wave to ask a buyer's question. Sections: what 1X Neo is and the ~$20,000 price and 2026 US-home shipping claim; what it can plausibly do at home vs demo-stage limits (teleoperation, safety, narrow tasks); the contrast with factory-first robots like Atlas; analyst caution that typical households won't get a useful robot soon. Verify Neo's price, ship timeline and any teleoperation caveats. Primary sources: eMarketer CES 2026 robots coverage; S&P Global CES physical-AI note; TechRadar CES 2026 trends.

topics.titleTr: Gemini Artık Sizin İçin İşletmeleri Arıyor
topics.titleEn: Gemini Can Now Call Businesses For You
topics.angle: deep-dive|explain Gemini's new on-your-behalf calling and what agentic phone tasks mean.
topics.brief: Open with Gemini phoning three shops to find an in-stock item. Sections: the Nov 2026 Pixel Drop feature letting Gemini call businesses using the owner's number to check inventory, hold items or manage reservations; which Pixel devices get it; etiquette and disclosure (does the business know it's an AI?); reliability limits and when to just call yourself; the broader agentic-assistant trend. Verify device support, the owner's-number detail and rollout. Primary sources: AndroidGuys / Android Police Pixel Drop coverage; Google Pixel feature-drop notes.

topics.angle: guide|cut CES 2026 hype down to the handful of trends worth a normal reader's attention.
topics.brief: A reader-first filter on CES 2026. Sections: smart glasses moving toward mass adoption (and display-less designs); AI wearables as a 'second brain', with smart rings as the cheaper, quieter bet; humanoid robots shifting from demo to early production; which of these a normal buyer should care about in 2026 vs wait on. Keep claims hedged as expectations, not shipped facts. Verify launch timelines and the display-less-glasses and ring claims. Primary sources: IDC and ABI Research CES 2026 analyses; TechRadar '11 biggest trends'; eMarketer CES recap.

topics.titleTr: ChatGPT Canlı Dikte: Yazmak Yerine Konuşun
topics.titleEn: ChatGPT Live Dictation: Talk Instead of Type
topics.angle: how-to|use the new faster, limit-free ChatGPT dictation to capture ideas by voice.
topics.brief: Open with capturing a messy idea on a walk and getting clean text back. Sections: what Live Dictation adds (Nov 18 2026, faster, rolling out to all plans on iOS, Android, web and desktop, reportedly no 10-minute recording cap); practical uses (voice journaling, drafting, meeting capture, accessibility); accuracy and privacy notes; pairing dictation with a cleanup prompt. Verify the no-limit claim, the plan/platform availability and date. Primary sources: OpenAI release notes; Releasebot ChatGPT tracker.

topics.titleEn: How to Raise a Series A in 2026
topics.angle: guide|a grounded playbook for raising a Series A in a concentrated, AI-tilted 2026 market.
topics.brief: Realistic Series A guide for a cooler, concentrated market. Sections: what's changed (capital pooling at the top, longer cycles, no single metric defining an A); traction and efficiency bars investors cite in 2026; building the raise 6+ months early; deal-term red flags (tranche financing); non-AI startups and the 'you don't have to become an AI company' nuance. Verify the Q2-2025 non-AI funding low and the tranche-financing warning. Primary sources: TechCrunch 'how founders can raise a Series A today'; Pilot H1-2026 VC report; PitchBook/Madrona commentary.

topics.titleTr: AI Yatırım Ayrışması: Doğru Pazara Sunum Yap
topics.titleEn: The AI Funding Split: Pitch the Right Market
topics.angle: deep-dive|explain the two-market split in venture and which story founders should actually tell.
topics.brief: Contrarian thesis: venture has split into AI and non-AI markets, and many founders pitch the wrong one. Sections: the evidence (AI's Series A valuation premium; non-AI investment at multi-year lows; froth concentrated at early/growth stages); how to position if you're AI-native vs AI-enabled vs deliberately not-AI; red flags of bubble-chasing; the durable-revenue counsel VCs keep repeating. Verify the valuation-premium and non-AI-low figures and the bubble-stage framing. Primary sources: CRV 'what investors look for 2026'; Fortune VC-concentration piece; GeekWire bubble roundtable.
